data.title: Transition
data.tagline: Smooth the change between two visual states
data.description: A transition animates a CSS property when its value changes, such as color on hover or a panel opening. Use it to clarify cause and effect, keep the duration short, and respect reduced-motion preferences. Not every property animates smoothly or cheaply.

use: Open or close a small panel
Help people follow a state change
avoid: Animate every property with one broad rule
Use a long transition for frequent controls
Animate layout-heavy properties without checking performance

lessonPractice.title: A switch thumb only needs to move smoothly between its on and off positions. Which implementation fits best?

options.label: Apply a short transition only to transform and respect reduced-motion preferences
options.feedback: The change has clear start and end states. Limiting the property avoids animating unrelated styles and respects motion preferences.

options.label: Set transition: all on the whole switch for one second
options.feedback: The all keyword can animate future color or size changes unintentionally, and one second slows direct feedback.

options.label: Write separate Open and Close keyframes and choose one for each state
options.feedback: Keyframes can move the thumb, but two directions duplicate maintenance when a transition already connects the current and next states.

data.agentPrompt: Move the switch thumb between its two positions with a short transition that names only transform and color, not transition: all. Remove nonessential motion for reduced-motion preferences and verify rapid toggling keeps the correct state.
